title: Indexes with Included Columns
description: Learn how to add non-key columns to non-clustered indexes to cover more queries and avoid key lookups.

data.text: SQL Server Indexes with Included Columns

By including non-key columns in non-clustered indexes, you can create nonclustered indexes that cover more queries. When an index contains all the columns referenced by a query, it is called a covering index.
When a non-clustered index does not contain all columns needed by a query, SQL Server performs a key lookup to fetch the missing columns from the clustered index or heap. This can be expensive.

data.title: Included Columns Key Points
points: Included columns are non-key columns added to a non-clustered index.
They allow the query optimizer to satisfy queries entirely from the index.
This avoids expensive key lookups to the clustered index or heap.
Use INCLUDE for columns frequently selected but not filtered on.
